verdict.rationale: Next.js documents familiar styling (CSS Modules, Tailwind, community libraries) and standard JavaScript async/await inside React components, and it auto-configures bundlers and compilers. However, components are written in React rather than plain markup, and community reports describe extra concepts to learn: confusion over browser, middleware, edge, node and SSR layers, and global functions like cookies() and headers() replacing request parameters. Missing for 10: evidence that components use standard HTML rather than React/JSX, evidence of a low concept count (server vs client boundaries add complexity), and independent corroboration of an easy learning curve.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write components using standard markup, styling, and language syntax I already know, minimizing new concepts to learn

citations.quote: Style your application with your favorite tools, including support for CSS Modules, Tailwind CSS, and popular community libraries.
Make your React component async and await your data.
It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers.
